summary: Specifies functions for MPLS Transport Profile OAM: continuity check to spot lost connectivity, connectivity verification to confirm source and sink match, and remote defect indication to report faults back to the other end. It was later updated by RFC 7214.

plainLanguage.summary: Like checking a phone call is still connected and you reached the right person, and telling them when you hear a problem. This sets those checks for transport paths in a network.

questions: how does bfd work with mpls-tp
subtitle: How MPLS-TP uses BFD to notice a dead path, check it is the right path, and tell the far end about a problem.

tldr.problem: Transport circuits built on MPLS need to detect lost continuity and mis-connectivity, and to report a fault back to the other end, just as traditional transport circuits do.
tldr.mechanism: Continuity Check (CC) and Connectivity Verification (CV) packets are interleaved in one Bidirectional Forwarding Detection (BFD) session, with new code points and a Source MEP-ID TLV on CV packets. Remote Defect Indication (RDI) rides in the BFD diagnostic code.
tldr.outcome: Sink end points can detect both silence and traffic arriving from the wrong place. The RFC is a Proposed Standard and was later updated by RFC 7214.

today: RFC 6428 is a Proposed Standard published in November 2011. It was later updated by RFC 7214, so read the two together.

sections.title: Why CC, CV and RDI
sections.content:
Service providers need OAM tools to detect mis-connectivity and loss of continuity of transport circuits. Pseudowires (PWs) and MPLS-TP Label Switched Paths (LSPs) that emulate such circuits must offer three functions, as RFC 5860 requires. Continuity Check (CC) monitors a path for loss of continuity. Connectivity Verification (CV) adds confirmation that the desired source is connected to the desired sink. Remote Defect Indication (RDI) lets one end point report to its peer that it sees a fault.

RFC 6428 builds all three on Bidirectional Forwarding Detection (BFD, RFC 5880), with extensions. It applies to PWs, LSPs, Sub-Path Maintenance Entities and Sections, between two Maintenance Entity Group End Points (MEPs). It supports co-routed and associated bidirectional LSPs and several encapsulations: GAL/G-ACh, VCCV and UDP/IP. It is restricted to BFD asynchronous mode, and procedures for unidirectional point-to-point and point-to-multipoint LSPs are left for further study.
sections.plainLanguage: Network operators need to know three things about a path. Is it still working? Is it the right one? And can the far end tell me when it sees trouble? This RFC answers all three with one small, repeating message.

sections.title: One BFD Session, Two Kinds of Packet
sections.content:
CC and CV are multiplexed within a single BFD session. Normal operation sends CC packets interleaved with CV packets. The two are told apart by distinct Associated Channel Header code points. The CV packet carries a Source MEP-ID TLV so the sink MEP can detect mis-connectivity. The insertion interval for CV packets is one per second.

A loss of continuity defect is declared when the time since the last received BFD control packet exceeds the detection time, which is the session periodicity times the remote system's Detect Multiplier. The Detect Multiplier is set to 3 for the CC code point. Mis-connectivity defects are detected in a maximum of one second.

RDI is not a separate packet. It is carried in the BFD diagnostic field of CC messages, and the diagnostic code in CV messages MUST be ignored. A sink MEP SHOULD send code 1 (Control Detection Time Expired) when the detection time passes with nothing received, SHOULD send code 5 (Path Down) after receiving a Link Down Indication, and MUST send code 9 (mis-connectivity defect) when CV processing finds mis-connectivity. A sink that has started sending code 5 SHOULD NOT change it to 1.

A CC-only mode already exists in RFC 5885 with ACH channel 7, and implementations may interoperate with legacy equipment using RFC 5884 for LSPs and RFC 5085 for PWs.
sections.plainLanguage: Most notes just say hello. Once a second, a note also carries a name tag. Trouble reports are written in a code on the hello note itself, so no extra note is needed.

sections.title: Code Points and Message Formats
sections.content:
Both message kinds start with a Generic Associated Channel header whose first nibble is 0001, with version and flags set to 0. The BFD CC code point is 0x0022 and the BFD proactive CV code point is 0x0023. A CC message is the ACH followed by a BFD control packet. A CV message is the ACH, the BFD control packet, and then a Source MEP-ID TLV. The length in the BFD control packet does not include that TLV.

The TLV has a 2-octet Type, a 2-octet Length and a variable Value, and a BFD session uses only one encoding. There are three types: 0 Section MEP-ID (global ID, node ID and interface number), 1 LSP MEP-ID (global ID, node ID, a 16-bit Tunnel_Num and a 16-bit LSP_Num), and 2 PW End Point MEP-ID (global ID, node ID, AC_ID and an Attachment Group Identifier). The identifiers come from RFC 6370.

When the GAL is used, its TTL MUST be at least 1 and it MUST be the end of stack label (S=1). A node MUST NOT change the Source MEP-ID TLV, and with digest-based authentication the TLV MUST NOT be included in the digest.
sections.plainLanguage: There are two note formats. The plain one is just the hello. The other has the sender's name tag stapled on, and nobody on the way is allowed to change the name tag.

sections.title: The BFD Profile for MPLS-TP
sections.content:
BFD runs in asynchronous mode with control packets sent periodically at a configurable rate, fixed and common to both directions for the life of the MEG. All packets MUST be sent with the M bit clear. A BFD session corresponds to a CC and proactive CV instance. It starts when an operator enables the functions, and goes to ADMIN DOWN and ends when they are disabled. All state changes and Poll/Final exchanges MUST use CC packets; this information in CV packets MUST be ignored.

There are two modes for bidirectional LSPs. In coordinated mode, one session covers both directions and its state tracks the defect state. In independent mode, two sessions run, and an independent session can be UP while receiving RDI. Independent mode is marked by the source MEP setting bfd.MinRxInterval to zero, with a sink MEP configured to a transmission interval of zero. RFC 6428 adds two clarifications for that case. When its state changes, a zero-rate MEP sends control messages once per second until the peer confirms the change. And the originating MEP ignores a DOWN state from a zero-interval peer, so the peer keeps sending DOWN with the RDI diagnostic code.

Sessions start with MinRx of 1 second, MinTx of at least 1 second and a detect multiplier of 3. Once UP, Poll/Final moves them to the desired rates, after which implementations SHOULD NOT try further rate changes. A peer may reject a new timer value by tearing down the session. Discriminators are local to the sink MEP or meaningless when unknown; My Discriminator MUST be non-zero and Your Discriminator MUST reflect the received value or be zero if unknown. Configuration and coordination of session parameters between MEPs is out of scope.
sections.plainLanguage: The two ends can either act as one team that agrees on everything, or each watch their own direction separately. Either way they begin by chatting once a second and then switch to the speed they want.

sections.title: Defects and State Machines
sections.content:
A MEP enters the defect state for CC when the BFD session times out (loss of continuity), or when it receives a Link Down Indication (defined in RFC 6427) or a Lock Report. It enters the mis-connectivity defect state when it sees any of these: an unexpected encapsulation (IP-encoded BFD on a GAL/G-ACh LSP, or the reverse); an unexpected Source MEP-ID; a Your Discriminator not in the local BFD database; a known discriminator with an unexpected label; or, if authentication is used, incorrect authentication information. The order of checking is: receiving nothing, then LDI or Lock Report, then an incorrect source, then a correct source with wrong session information, then all correct.

On defect entry a sink MEP asserts signal fail into client layers and signals session DOWN to its peer using CC messages. Traffic blocking MUST follow only what RFC 6371 specifies. For mis-connectivity, the termination silently discards non-OAM traffic and the sink MEP reports diagnostic code 9. A mis-connectivity defect clears when no defective CV messages have arrived for 3.5 seconds. A loss of continuity defect in an independent session clears on receipt of a well-formed control packet from the peer.

The RFC updates the RFC 5880 state machines to take LDI and, optionally, Lock Report as inputs. In a coordinated session in the UP state, LDI or an optional Lock Report moves the session to DOWN. In independent mode, the source MEP never leaves UP except by forced ADMIN DOWN, and the sink MEP may go straight from DOWN to UP once initialized.
sections.plainLanguage: If the notes stop coming, or a note comes from the wrong sender, the receiver says so and stops trusting the path. Once good notes arrive again, or a few seconds pass with no bad ones, it calms down.

sections.title: Security Considerations
sections.content:
CV improves network integrity by ensuring traffic is not leaking between LSPs. BFD's optional authentication can be used here. Although the Source MEP-ID TLV is outside the authentication digest, a chain of trust links the discriminator in the digest to the expected MEP-ID, which prevents impersonation of CV messages.

The RFC specifies globally unique MEP-IDs, which gives authoritative detection of persistent leaking. If two LSPs with common MEP-IDs are misconnected, the leak could go undetected. The RFC calls this undesirable but rare, and hard to exploit because both a network end point and a transit node of the target MEG would need to be compromised.
sections.plainLanguage: The name tags are meant to be unique, like fingerprints. Fooling the check would need a bad actor in two places at once, which is very hard.

sections.title: IANA Assignments
sections.content: IANA allocated two channel types from the Pseudowire Associated Channel Types registry: 0x0022 for the MPLS-TP CC message and 0x0023 for the MPLS-TP CV message. It created a CC/CV MEP-ID TLV registry under it, allocated by Standards Action, with initial values 0 (Section MEP-ID), 1 (LSP MEP-ID) and 2 (PW MEP-ID). It also assigned BFD diagnostic code 9, mis-connectivity defect, in the BFD Diagnostic Codes subregistry.
sections.plainLanguage: The special numbers used by these messages are written in the official list so no one else reuses them.
